title: GA Blocker Resolution

outputs.root_cause: _redactSecrets used replaceFirstMapped, so only the first match of each pattern was redacted; a second credential of the same class was written to the crash artifact in full.
outputs.risk_update: Any crash message carrying two same-class credentials retained the second one on disk until the next app data purge.
outputs.release_note: Crash artifacts no longer retain a second same-class credential.

outputs.root_cause: The sink kept its own copy of the provider-token patterns and that copy had drifted from the canonical SecretScanner: it required a DASH separator, so the real GitHub formats (ghp_, github_pat_) and Slack xoxb- never matched, and it had no AKIA family at all.
outputs.fix: The sink now delegates shape detection to the canonical SecretScanner instead of holding a private list.
outputs.review: 5 families measured; all recognised by the canonical scanner and all redacted in the crash artifact.
outputs.risk_update: Credentials named by our own archive guard were never candidates for crash-artifact redaction; that class of leak is now closed at the source of truth.
outputs.release_note: Crash sink now covers every credential family the archive guard already recognises, and can no longer drift from it.

claim_boundary: No GA blocker was filed by a participant and no live release is claimed. The beta cohort has not started. Both defects were measured against the shipped crash sink on state owned by the test, not against a live cohort. Domains outside domains_measured remain unresolved and are NOT closed by this run.
external_gates: DEFERRED-EXTERNAL: live beta cohort, real credential exposure, hosted CI, signing, publication.
